correctness.rationale: For every factor, the all-block count recurrence has error at most i+k-1. Its weighted series converges absolutely and gives a bound i+k on each finite-stage scaled discrepancy. For every prefix, two bounded boundary corrections lead to a recurrence with next argument at most 2N/3, giving O_k(log^2 N). The known recurrence theorem permits far-right occurrences; they double through r-t stages and the resulting count dominates the remaining negative series tail, making each admissible factor frequency positive. Shift invariance follows from extension counts. The attached checker independently corroborates finite boundary identities, without being used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: For the recently studied nonuniformly recurrent, exponentially complex word, single-letter density does not control higher-factor statistical frequencies and recurrence does not imply positive density. The theorem proves existence, strict positivity, efficient rational enclosures, and quantitative genericity for a full-support invariant golden-mean measure. It is an infinite structural property of the natural source object, not a finite census or routine reparameterization.
